Robust and sparse group-level DCM

Source: R/rsDCM.R
rsdcm.Rd

Fits a group model to subject-level DCM posterior means and covariances. The likelihood is Student-t after block-covariance pre-whitening. Group coefficients receive a Gaussian-spike and nonlocal pMOM-slab prior.

rsdcm(
  eta_theta_y,
  C_theta_y_list,
  X_G,
  V_list,
  nu = 3,
  tau0 = 0.05,
  tau1 = 1,
  pi = 0.4,
  a0 = 2,
  b0 = 0.01,
  a1 = 2,
  b1 = 1,
  min_slab_spike_ratio = 1,
  max_iter = 200,
  tol = 1e-06,
  inner_sweeps = 3,
  verbose = TRUE,
  max_beta_step = 1,
  min_alpha = 1e-08,
  max_alpha = 100,
  whitening_method = c("precision_chol", "covariance_chol", "symmetric"),
  estimate_sigma2 = FALSE,
  sigma2_fixed = 1,
  beta_init = NULL,
  alpha_init = NULL,
  n_starts = 3L,
  start_jitter = 0.25,
  start_seed = NULL,
  objective_tol = 1e-10,
  gradient_tol = 1e-04,
  max_backtrack = 20L,
  pip_all_starts = FALSE,
  pip_mcmc_iter = 10000L,
  pip_mcmc_burn = 3000L,
  pip_mcmc_thin = 2L,
  pip_mcmc_chains = 4L,
  pip_mcmc_temperatures = 8L,
  pip_mcmc_min_inverse_temp = 0.05,
  pip_mcmc_swap_every = 2L,
  pip_mcmc_large_jump_prob = 0.1,
  pip_mcmc_seed = NULL
)

Arguments

eta_theta_y

Numeric N by p matrix of subject-level posterior means.

C_theta_y_list

Length-N list of p by p posterior covariance matrices.

X_G

Numeric N by r between-subject design matrix.

V_list

List of symmetric p by p bases defining \(\Sigma_b=\sum_k\alpha_k V_k\). The matrices must be linearly independent.

nu

Positive Student-t degrees of freedom.

tau0, tau1

Initial spike and slab standard deviations.

pi

Prior slab probability in (0, 1).

a0, b0, a1, b1

Inverse-Gamma hyperparameters for the squared spike and slab scales.

min_slab_spike_ratio

Minimum allowed ratio tau1/tau0.

max_iter

Maximum generalized-EM iterations per start.

tol

Relative parameter and objective convergence tolerance.

inner_sweeps

Number of coordinate-Newton sweeps in each conditional maximization of the group effects.

verbose

Logical. Print fitting and MCMC diagnostics.

max_beta_step

Maximum absolute coordinate-Newton step.

min_alpha, max_alpha

Bounds for covariance-component amplitudes.

whitening_method

Pre-whitening factorization. One of "precision_chol", "covariance_chol", or "symmetric".

estimate_sigma2

Logical. Estimate the global residual scale. The default fixes it to avoid confounding with covariance-component scale.

sigma2_fixed

Positive residual scale used when estimate_sigma2 = FALSE.

beta_init, alpha_init

Optional initial coefficient and covariance- component vectors.

n_starts

Number of empirical-Bayes starts.

start_jitter

Standard deviation multiplier for randomized starts.

start_seed

Optional random seed for randomized starts.

objective_tol

Numerical tolerance for monotonicity safeguards.

gradient_tol

Maximum coefficient-score norm required for convergence.

max_backtrack

Maximum backtracking halvings for a coefficient update.

pip_all_starts

Logical. Compute integrated PIPs for every start rather than only the selected start.

pip_mcmc_iter, pip_mcmc_burn, pip_mcmc_thin

Parallel-tempering MCMC iteration, burn-in, and thinning settings.

pip_mcmc_chains

Number of independent temperature ladders.

pip_mcmc_temperatures

Number of replicas in each ladder.

pip_mcmc_min_inverse_temp

Inverse temperature of the hottest replica.

pip_mcmc_swap_every

Number of iterations between replica swaps.

pip_mcmc_large_jump_prob

Probability of a slab-scale proposal.

pip_mcmc_seed

Optional random seed for posterior PIP integration.

Value

A list containing empirical-Bayes modes beta_mat, conditional posterior means beta_posterior_mean, conditional Laplace standard deviations beta_sd_approx, integrated PIPs inclusion, PIP Monte Carlo errors and chain diagnostics, Student-t weights, fitted scales and covariance components, convergence traces, multistart diagnostics, whitening information, and fitted subject-level means.

Details

Mode fitting uses multistart generalized expectation-maximization with conditional maximization. Integrated posterior inclusion probabilities (PIPs) are then computed by parallel-tempering MCMC while holding the empirical-Bayes hyperparameters fixed. The returned coefficient standard deviations use a conditional Laplace approximation at the selected mode.

The Student-t weights apply to residual coordinates defined by the selected whitening factor and the supplied parameter ordering. They are not invariant to arbitrary rotations of the whitened coordinates.

References

Johnson, V. E. and Rossell, D. (2010). On the use of non-local prior densities in Bayesian hypothesis tests. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 72(2), 143–170.

See also

rsdcm_fit, dcm_peb_run

Examples

set.seed(1)
N <- 12L
p <- 3L
X_G <- matrix(1, N, 1, dimnames = list(NULL, "intercept"))
eta <- matrix(rnorm(N * p, sd = 0.25), N, p)
eta[, 1] <- eta[, 1] + 0.7
colnames(eta) <- paste0("P", seq_len(p))
Cp <- replicate(N, diag(0.1, p), simplify = FALSE)
V <- lapply(seq_len(p), function(j) {
  z <- matrix(0, p, p)
  z[j, j] <- 1
  z
})
# \donttest{
fit <- rsdcm(
  eta, Cp, X_G, V, n_starts = 1L, max_iter = 100L,
  pip_mcmc_iter = 1000L, pip_mcmc_burn = 400L,
  pip_mcmc_thin = 5L, pip_mcmc_chains = 2L,
  pip_mcmc_temperatures = 4L, verbose = FALSE
)
cbind(fit$beta_mat, PIP = fit$inclusion[, 1])
#>       intercept         PIP
#> P1  0.764428748 1.000000000
#> P2  0.011277761 0.005746535
#> P3 -0.005717361 0.001908935
# }
